newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal declines comment on soccer clubs tax probe.
newsitem.headline: Portugal declines comment on soccer clubs tax probe.

text.p: A senior Portuguese official on Thursday declined comment on a newspaper report that authorities were investigating 38 leading soccer clubs for possible tax evasion.

"I can't confirm or deny the report," Jose Martins de Sa, Inspector-General of Finance, told Reuters when asked to confirm a report in Publico that authorities were investigating the tax affairs of 38 clubs in the first and second divisions.
Portugal's opposition severely embarrassed the government in June when it rejected a state plan to bail out heavily indebted soccer clubs.
Portugal's soccer clubs are estimated to owe $100 million in back taxes and social security payments, officials say.
The debts of the clubs are only a drop in the ocean when compared to one trillion escudos ($6.4 billion) owed by private citizens and companies in taxes and unpaid social security dues.
